modern: These two things can’t be separated: abiding in obedience and abiding in the love of Jesus. Only a life under the rule of Christ can prove that we are the ones our Lord delights in. We must keep our Lord’s command if we want to bask in his love. If we live in sin, we can’t live in the love of Christ. Without the holiness that pleases God, we can’t please Jesus. Whoever cares nothing for holiness knows nothing of the love of Jesus.

Feeling and enjoying our Lord’s love is a delicate thing. It is far more sensitive to sin and holiness than the mercury in a thermometer is to cold and heat. When we are tender of heart, and careful in thought, word and life to honor our Lord Jesus, we receive countless tokens of his love. If we want that joy to last, our holiness must last. The Lord Jesus won’t hide his face from us unless we hide our face from him. Sin makes the cloud that darkens our Sun. If we are watchfully obedient and completely given over to him, we may walk in the light, as God is in the light, and be as surely at home in the love of Jesus as Jesus is in the love of the Father. Here is a sweet promise with a solemn “if.” Lord, let me hold this “if” in my hand; for like a key it opens this treasure chest.

notes.term: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love
notes.note: “…even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love” ([[John.15.10|John 15:10]]). To abide is to remain, to make your home.
The liquid metal in a thermometer, which rises and falls with the slightest change in temperature.
Make something last.
Set apart for God.

notes.term: Walk in the light, as God is in the light
notes.note: “But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another” ([[1John.1.7|1 John 1:7]]).
A small box for jewels or valuables, not a coffin.

modern: We will reach holy knowledge not all at once but step by step, and our business is to persevere and learn little by little. We don’t need to despair, though our progress may be slow, for we will know in the end. The Lord, who has become our Teacher, won’t give up on us, however slow to understand we may be; for it wouldn’t be to his honor if any amount of human foolishness defeated his skill. The Lord delights to make the simple wise.

Our duty is to stick to our main subject, and follow on to know, not this particular doctrine or that one, but Jehovah himself. To know Father, Son and Spirit, the triune God: this is eternal life. Let’s keep to this, for this is the way we will gain a complete education. By following on to know the Lord, we learn healing after being torn, binding up after being struck, and life after death. Experience does its perfect work when the heart follows the track of the Almighty Lord.

My soul, keep close to Jesus; follow on to know God in Jesus, and so you will come to the knowledge of Christ, the most excellent of all the sciences. The Holy Spirit will lead you into all truth. Isn’t this his gracious office? Rely on him to fulfill it.

notes.term: Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord
notes.note: [[Hos.6.3|Hosea 6:3]]. The verse goes on: “his going forth is prepared as the morning.”

notes.term: The Lord delights to make the simple wise
notes.note: “The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple” ([[Ps.19.7|Psalm 19:7]]).
Special, belonging particularly to someone (not odd). Here, one particular doctrine.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Three in one: one God in three persons.
“And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent” ([[John.17.3|John 17:3]]).
“Come, and let us return unto the LORD: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up” ([[Hos.6.1|Hosea 6:1]]).
An echo of “let patience have her perfect work” ([[Jas.1.4|James 1:4]]).

notes.term: The most excellent of all the sciences
notes.note: Science in the old sense: any branch of knowledge. Paul counted everything loss “for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord” ([[Phil.3.8|Philippians 3:8]]).

notes.term: The Holy Ghost will lead thee into all truth
notes.note: “Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth” ([[John.16.13|John 16:13]]).
An appointed task or duty.

modern: It must be so: those who receive life from the dead are sure to recognize the hand of the Lord in such a resurrection. This is the greatest and most remarkable change a person can go through: to be brought out of the grave of spiritual death, and made to rejoice in the light and freedom of spiritual life. No one could do this but the living God, the Lord and giver of life.

Oh, how well I remember when I was lying in the valley full of dry bones, as dry as any of them! Blessed was the day when free and sovereign grace sent the man of God to prophesy over me! Glory be to God for the stir that word of faith caused among the dry bones. More blessed still was that heavenly breath from the four winds that made me live! Now I know the life-giving Spirit of the ever-living Jehovah. Truly Jehovah is the living God, for he made me live. My new life, even in its longings and sorrows, is clear proof to me that the Lord can kill and make alive. He is the only God. He is all that is great, gracious and glorious, and my soul, made alive, adores him as the great I AM. All glory be to his sacred name! As long as I live I will praise him.

notes.term: When I have opened your graves
notes.note: From Ezekiel’s vision of the valley of dry bones, which came to life when he prophesied and the breath of God entered them ([[Ezek.37.1-Ezek.37.14|Ezekiel 37:1–14]]).

notes.term: The Lord and giver of life
notes.note: From the Nicene Creed, which calls the Holy Spirit “the Lord, and Giver of life.”
God’s right and power to rule and to choose freely, answering to no one.

notes.term: The man of God to prophesy upon me
notes.note: Ezekiel was told, “Prophesy upon these bones” ([[Ezek.37.4|Ezekiel 37:4]]). Spurgeon means the preacher God sent to him.
“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live” ([[Ezek.37.9|Ezekiel 37:9]]).
To make alive. “Quick” once meant “living”, as in “the quick and the dead”.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Longings.

notes.term: The Lord can kill and make alive
notes.note: “The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up” ([[1Sam.2.6|1 Samuel 2:6]]).
The name God gave Moses at the burning bush: “I AM THAT I AM” ([[Exod.3.14|Exodus 3:14]]).

modern: A precious word! Jehovah himself will rescue his people in the greatness of his mercy, but he won’t do it by the ordinary means. People are slow to give God the glory due to his name. If they go to battle with sword and bow and win the victory, they ought to praise their God; yet they don’t, but start praising their own right arm, and boasting in their horses and horsemen. For this reason our Jehovah often decides to save his people without any go-betweens, so that all the honor may be his alone.

Look, then, my heart, to the Lord alone, and not to man. Expect to see God all the more clearly when there is no one else to look to. If I have no friend, no adviser, no one backing me, let me be no less confident if I can feel that the Lord himself is on my side. Yes, let me be glad if he gives victory without a battle, as the text seems to suggest. Why do I ask for horses and horsemen if Jehovah himself has mercy on me, and lifts up his arm to defend me? Why do I need bow or sword if God will save? Let me trust and not be afraid, from this day on and for evermore. Amen.

notes.term: Will not save them by bow, nor by sword
notes.note: [[Hos.1.7|Hosea 1:7]]. God kept this word when he struck down the Assyrian army camped against Jerusalem in a single night, without a battle ([[2Kgs.19.35|2 Kings 19:35]]).
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Give.

notes.term: The glory due unto His name
notes.note: “Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name” ([[Ps.29.2|Psalm 29:2]]).
Praise; make much of.
The ordinary people and things God works through, such as soldiers and weapons.
“Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid” ([[Isa.12.2|Isaiah 12:2]]).

modern: This was a great mercy for Jehoshaphat, for a huge army had come out against him; and it will be a great mercy for me, for I am in great need, and I have no strength or wisdom. If the Lord is with me, it matters little who deserts me. If the Lord is with me, I will win the battle of life, and the greater my trials, the more glorious my victory will be. How can I be sure the Lord is with me?

He is certainly with me if I am with him. If I trust his faithfulness, believe his words and obey his commands, he is surely with me. If I am on Satan’s side, God is against me, and can’t be anything else; but if I live to honor God, I can be sure he will honor me.

I am quite sure God is with me if Jesus is my one and only Savior. If I have put my soul into the hands of God’s only begotten Son, then I can be sure the Father will use all his power to keep me safe, so that his Son is not dishonored.

Oh, for faith to take hold of the short but sweet text for today! O Lord, keep this word to your servant! Be with me in the house, in the street, in the field, in the shop, in company and alone. Be with all your people too.

notes.term: The Lord will be with you
notes.note: The prophet Jahaziel to King Jehoshaphat, when a vast army from Moab, Ammon and Mount Seir came against Judah: “Ye shall not need to fight in this battle” ([[2Chr.20.15-2Chr.20.17|2 Chronicles 20:15–17]]).

notes.term: If I live to honor God I may be sure that He will honor me
notes.note: “For them that honour me I will honour” ([[1Sam.2.30|1 Samuel 2:30]]).
One and only: God’s unique Son ([[John.3.16|John 3:16]]).
Use; bring into play.

modern: Wait! Wait! Let your waiting be on the Lord! He is worth waiting for. He never disappoints the soul that waits.
While you wait, keep your spirits up. Expect a great rescue, and be ready to praise God for it.

The promise that should cheer you is in the middle of the verse: “He shall strengthen thine heart.” This goes straight to the place where you need help. If the heart is sound, all the rest of the body will work well. The heart needs calming and cheering, and both will come if it is strengthened. A strong heart rests and rejoices, and pumps strength into the whole person.

No one else can reach that secret urn of life, the heart, to pour strength into it. Only the one who made it can make it strong. God is full of strength, and so he can give it to those who need it. Oh, be brave; for the Lord will give you his strength, and you will be calm in the storm and glad in sorrow.
The one who wrote these lines can write as David did: “Wait, I say, on the Lord.” I do indeed say it. I know by long and deep experience that it is good for me to wait on the Lord.

notes.note: [[Ps.27.14|Psalm 27:14]]. To wait on the Lord is to look to him in hope and trust until he acts.
Be brave.
The body as a whole.
A vase or jar; here, the vessel that holds life itself.
Give, share.
Wrote.

notes.term: It is good for me to wait upon the Lord
notes.note: “It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD” ([[Lam.3.26|Lamentations 3:26]]).

modern: Sovereign grace can turn strangers into sons, and here the Lord declares that he means to deal with rebels in this way and make them know what he has done. Dear reader, the Lord has done this in my case; has he done the same for you? Then let’s join hands and hearts in praising his adorable name.

Some of us were so plainly ungodly that the Lord’s Word said, most truly, to our conscience and heart, “Ye are not my people.” In the house of God, and in our own homes when we read the Bible, this was the voice of God’s Spirit in our soul: “Ye are not my people.” It was a sad, condemning voice indeed. But now, in the same places, through the same preaching and Scripture, we hear a voice that says, “Ye are the sons of the living God.” Can we ever be grateful enough for this? Isn’t it wonderful? Doesn’t it give us hope for others? Who is beyond the reach of almighty grace? How can we despair of anyone, since the Lord has worked such a marvelous change in us?
The one who has kept this one great promise will keep every other; so let’s go forward with songs of worship and confidence.

notes.note: God told Hosea to name his son Lo-ammi, “Not my people,” as a sign against Israel ([[Hos.1.9|Hosea 1:9]]), then promised this reversal. Paul applies it to Gentiles called by grace ([[Rom.9.25-Rom.9.26|Romans 9:25–26]]).
God’s right and power to rule and to choose freely, answering to no one.
Worthy of worship (not merely charming).
The preaching of the Word.
Worked.
So, therefore.
